name: who
description: Shows who is logged into the system, from which terminal, and since when.

flags.description: Time of the last system boot.
Include idle time and process ID.
All information (boot time, runlevel, dead sessions).
Show only your own session (who am i).

examples.explanation: Two sessions: a local graphical login (tty7) and alice over SSH from 10.0.0.24.
When the machine was last booted.
Your own current session — useful after multiple su/sudo hops.

about: who reads /var/run/utmp, which records login sessions. It is different from w, which also shows what each user is doing (current command, CPU time), and from last, which reads the historical log /var/log/wtmp.
useCases: See who else is on a shared server before rebooting or updating.
Find which terminal your session is on.
mistakes: Expecting who to show historical logins — that is last.
